$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] $$ Write down the expression that gives the solution of the initial value problem above. *Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & t{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$*
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,+{\int }_{0}^{t}\,\,$ $(t-s){e}^{4t}$ $\,\,\text{d}s$
${e}^{4t}$ {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & t{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}].$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At}\,x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & t{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{4(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{4(t-s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{4(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{4(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{4s}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(t-s){e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]+{\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}(t-s){e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-1)}\,x(1) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) \\ 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$

$x(t)=\,\,$ $2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-1))$ $\,\,+{\int }_{1}^{t}\,\,$ ${e}^{6s}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s))$ $\,\,\text{d}s$

questions.worked_solution:
Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}].$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-1)}\,x(1) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-1)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-1)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-1)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-1))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-1)) \\ 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-1))+\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-1))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-s)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-s))\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-s)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-s))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{6s}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{6s}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6(t-s)) \\ {e}^{6s}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(6(t-s))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
